questions.q: The little boy did many mischiefs in school.
questions.s:
The correct answer is: "made much mischief"

  • "Mischief" is an uncountable noun and does not have a plural form. Therefore, you should not use "mischiefs."

  • The correct phrase is "made much mischief".

Correct sentence: The little boy made much mischief in school.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

A ________ of bees swarmed around the blooming flowers.
questions.s:
The error is in the formation of the possessive for the compound noun 'Commander-in-Chief'. To show possession, the apostrophe and 's' ('s) should be added to the very end of the entire compound noun, not to the principal word within it.

Option a) 'Commanders-in-Chief's orders' is a plural possessive, implying the orders came from multiple commanders, which doesn't fit the singular context suggested by 'the'.

Option b) 'Commander-in-Chiefs' orders' is an incorrectly formed plural possessive.

Option c) 'Commanders-in-Chief orders' is plural but not possessive. It lacks the apostrophe needed to show that the orders belong to the commander.

Option d) 'Commander-in-Chief's orders' correctly forms the singular possessive by adding 's at the end of the full title.

The correct sentence is: The soldiers immediately followed the Commander-in-Chief's orders to mobilize the troops and secure the border, demonstrating their unwavering discipline and readiness for the important mission ahead.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Possessive nouns: are types of nouns that show ownership or connection. All nouns become possessive nouns with the addition of an apostrophe and a suffix - the letter "s" - at the end of the word. For compound nouns, the possessive marker is added to the last word.

questions.q: Srilekha is Mr. Singhs daughter.
questions.s:
Ans (c) Explanation:-

Mr singh ka daughter noun pe possession bnana hai isliye apostrophe ka use hoga. A option ke possession nhi hai isliye wo galat hai. Mr Singh singular person hai isliye B and D option galat hai. C option - Mr. Singh's daughter grammatically sahi hai.

questions.q: My friend Jatin usually wears a spectacle. MTS 19/07/2022 S1
questions.s: Replace 'a spectacle' with 'spectacles'. The word for eyeglasses is always plural: "spectacles" or "a pair of spectacles."

questions.q: The political candidate canvassed the neighborhood, going doors to doors to talk to voters.
o: going door to doors to talk to voters
questions.s:
In this sentence, "doors to doors" is incorrect. The correct phrase is "door to door," indicating movement from one door to another. When a preposition comes after a noun and then the same noun is repeated, the noun should be used in a singular form.

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "The political candidate canvassed the neighborhood, going door to door to talk to voters."

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no improvement required, select ‘No improvement’.
questions.s:
Solution:
The underlined phrase "come along the way" is incorrect.
The correct idiom is "come a long way", which means to have made significant progress or improvement over time.

So, the correct sentence should be:
"Sherpas have prospered and come a long way from being just porters to becoming mountaineers."

Option A: come a long way – correct idiomatic usage
Option B: are coming along – incorrect tense and idiom
Option C: come all along – incorrect expression
Option D: No improvement – incorrect due to misuse of idiom

Answer: Option A (come a long way).

questions.q: These kind/(a) of shirts are rather expensive/(b) for him to buy /(c) no error/(d)
o: of shirts are rather expensive
for him to buy
questions.s: The error is in part (a) because "these" is a plural determiner, so the noun that follows it must also be plural, making the correct phrase "These kinds of shirts".

questions.q:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'.

Ben Essenburg is widely known / as one of the world's best portrayer / of the Everglades.
o: as one of the world's best portrayer
questions.s:
The phrase 'one of the' is followed by the plural nouns, whereas 'portrayer' is the singular noun.

The correct sentence is: Ben Essenburg is widely known as one of the world's best portrayers of the Everglades.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.q: The tourist was relieved to discover that the pick pocketer had failed to steal anything from his pocket.
questions.s:
The term "pick pocketer" is incorrect. The correct term is "pickpocket."

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "The tourist was relieved to discover that the pickpocket had failed to steal anything from his pocket."

questions.q: The first innings/ of the match/were very sensational./no error
questions.s:
The word “innings” is singular in cricket (and remains the same in plural).
Since we are talking about “The first innings”, that’s one innings, so the verb must be singular.
Correct Sentence:The first innings of the match was very sensational.

questions.s: Replace 'two dozens' with 'two dozen'. After a number, "dozen" remains singular: "two dozen mangoes" (not "two dozens").
